caption: The drawing depicts the interior elevation of a small building with a gabled roof structure shown in an angled perspective, colored mainly in brown, red, blue, and white. The roof is shaded with diagonal brown and gray lines to suggest wooden beams. The wall is primarily white. The upper section is bordered by a decorative frieze consisting of alternating red oval and blue circular shapes, with a blue stripe running just below it following the contour of the roof. There are three prominent arched niches in the wall: the central arch is the largest, flanked by two smaller arches, all decorated with red and blue columns and arches. The central arched niche is more ornate, combining blue and red scalloped outlines, and contains a painted vase with stylized leaves in blue and red. The side arches each house a rosette motif composed of blue round shapes. Below these, on the left, there is a rectangular door with a grid-patterned opening at the top and blue diamond designs on the bottom panels. The floor is depicted in reddish-brown, mimicking tiles. Red vertical lines of small leaf shapes run from below each arch and at the far sides, and two empty rectangular frames with decorative red borders are centrally placed on the mid-level of the wall. The artist’s signature appears in the lower right corner.
title: Wall Painting (Reredos)
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
